prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To compute an actual dollar range we need: (1) the monthly rent amount under the renewed 2018 lease, so the nine months of claimed unpaid rent can be calculated; (2) the actual dollar total of late fees Edgemere is claiming (the 10%-per-month-plus-$50-per-day formula applied over the relevant period); (3) the dollar amount of the security deposit Edgemere retained; (4) any concrete lost-profit calculation for Lawal's practice (e.g., lost patient revenue, missed procedure billings) rather than only subjective testimony; (5) the actual cost Lawal incurred setting up his new office; and (6) the attorney's fees each side has actually incurred or is claiming.
prediction.likelyOutcome: On the current record, Edgemere's unpaid-rent claim is a genuine toss-up given its own unretracted termination notice and Lawal's own negotiated departure timeline, while Lawal's constructive eviction, quiet enjoyment, lost-profit, and relocation-cost counterclaims are weak given the absence of any physical interference and his year-long continued occupancy. The most likely net outcome is a split verdict: Edgemere recovers a reduced rent/late-fee award (discounted for mitigation problems and a vulnerable penalty clause) while Lawal recovers the wrongfully withheld security deposit, with fee-shifting following whichever side comes out net ahead. No reliable dollar figure can be assigned, however, without the missing economic data.

issues.label: Edgemere's Unpaid Rent Claim (9 Months Post-Vacatur)
Failure to Mitigate Damages (Nine-Month Reletting Delay)
Breach of Implied Warranty of Quiet Enjoyment
Cost of Setting Up New Office

outcome.description: The jury found for the tenant on all claims and the trial court entered judgment for $36,791.80 moving expenses, $42,000 lost profits and $5,000 for the retained security deposit (total $83,791.80), plus $67,000 attorney's fees, interest and costs, and took-nothing on the landlord's rent claim. The court of appeals reversed the constructive-eviction/implied-warranty recovery (no evidence of substantial interference) and rendered judgment that the tenant take nothing on those claims, affirmed the judgment against the landlord on its breach claim and for the tenant on the $5,000 security-deposit claim, and remanded attorney's fees for a new trial.
outcome.finalNote: Reduced on appeal to the $5,000 security deposit.
